pages.page_summary: The page contains a series of physics problems (5.9 through 5.16) covering topics such as power, work, kinetic energy, and collisions. It concludes with a diagram (Fig. 5.14) illustrating three possible outcomes for an elastic collision between three identical ball bearings.
knowledge_points: Problem 5.9 asks for the proportionality of power delivered to a body with constant acceleration to time t.
Problem 5.10 asks for the proportionality of displacement to time t for a body moving under constant power.
Problem 5.11 involves calculating work done by a constant force F = -i + 2j + 3k N on a body moving 4 m along the z-axis.
Problem 5.12 compares the speeds of an electron (10 keV) and a proton (100 keV) and asks for the ratio of their speeds.
Problem 5.13 describes a rain drop falling with viscous resistance, asking for work done by gravity and resistive force.
Problem 5.14 asks about momentum conservation and elasticity for a gas molecule hitting a wall at 30 degrees.
Problem 5.15 calculates electric power consumed by a pump filling a tank of 30 m³ volume at 40 m height with 30% efficiency.
Problem 5.16 asks to identify the possible result of an elastic collision between three identical ball bearings as shown in Fig. 5.14.

embedded_text.visual_description: Diagram showing initial state and three possible outcomes (i, ii, iii) for a collision of three ball bearings.

visuals.description: A schematic diagram illustrating an elastic collision scenario. On the left, ball bearing 1 (blue) moves with velocity V towards ball bearings 2 (black) and 3 (light blue) which are in contact and at rest. Three arrows point to three possible outcomes labeled (i), (ii), and (iii). In (i), ball 1 stops (V=0) and balls 2 and 3 move together with velocity V/2. In (ii), balls 1 and 2 stop (V=0) and ball 3 moves with velocity V. In (iii), all three balls move together with velocity V/3.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates the conservation of momentum and kinetic energy in a 1D elastic collision involving multiple identical masses.
